newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends mixed on auction forecast shift.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends mixed on auction forecast shift.

text.p: The Mexican peso ended mixed on Tuesday, after zigzagging through the session on fluctuating U.S. long bond yields and forecasts for domestic primary auction rates, traders said.
"Dealers decided to go with the (U.S.) long bond at the close, but they also tried to sell dollars they had bought this morning as money market rates looked strong," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso ended 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.9590/7.9630 per dollar, while its 24-hour stablemate closed unchanged at 7.9550/7.9590 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.8 centavos weaker at 7.9660/7.9710 per dollar.
"I see high interest rates, so maybe that is why dealers sold off some dollars," another trader said.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders nN11527106 in Mexico City showed they forecast Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average rate of 22.09 percent. This would be an increase of 93 basis points from last week's auction.
Traders said the 48-hour peso opened strong and weakened by midday, before recovering at the close on wavering U.S. long bond yields.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds stood at 6.82 percent when the Mexican foreign exchange market opened, rose to 6.86 percent and receded to 6.84 percent by the close.
